title: Amazon SQS
description: Learn to use Amazon Simple Queue Service for decoupled, asynchronous communication between microservices.

data.text: Amazon Simple Queue Service (SQS) is a fully managed message queuing service. It lets you decouple distributed systems and build microservices. Instead of calling services directly, you send messages to a queue, and the receiving service processes them at its own pace.
SQS offers two types of queues, each with different guarantees.

When a consumer receives a message from the queue, it is hidden from other consumers for a period called the visibility timeout. If the consumer does not delete the message before the timeout expires, the message becomes visible again. If a message fails repeatedly, it can be moved to a Dead-Letter Queue (DLQ) for later inspection.

Long polling reduces empty responses by having the queue wait up to 20 seconds for a message to arrive. Message retention lets you keep messages in the queue for up to 14 days, which is useful for replay or debugging.

data.title: Use FIFO for Critical Data
data.text: Use FIFO queues when order matters and you cannot afford duplicates. Examples include banking transactions and order processing.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: SQS decouples producers from consumers for resilient systems
Standard queues offer unlimited throughput; FIFO queues guarantee order
Use DLQs to capture messages that cannot be processed
Long polling reduces cost and latency
data.takeaway: SQS is the simplest way to make your microservices resilient. If one service is down, messages wait in the queue until it comes back online.
